birkenbihl.title: much, many, a lot of, some, any – Beispielsätze

sentences.en: There isn't much water in the bottle.
sentences.de: In der Flasche ist nicht viel Wasser. (much + unzählbar, in Verneinung/Frage)
Er hat nicht viele Tassen. (many + zählbar, in Verneinung/Frage)

sentences.en: There are a lot of people in the park.
sentences.de: Im Park sind viele Leute. (a lot of = bejahter Satz, zählbar UND unzählbar)

sentences.en: She bought some milk from the store.
sentences.de: Sie hat im Geschäft etwas Milch gekauft. (some = bejahter Satz)
Ist noch Kaffee übrig? (any = Frage und Verneinung)

sentences.en: There is no cake left! Ben's eaten the whole thing!
sentences.de: Es ist kein Kuchen mehr übrig! Ben hat alles aufgegessen! (no + Nomen = kein)
Sie hat sehr wenige Freunde. (few + zählbar = wenige, negativ gemeint)

sentences.en: We've got very little petrol left.
sentences.de: Wir haben nur noch sehr wenig Benzin. (little + unzählbar = wenig, negativ gemeint)

sentences.en: We stayed a few days in Florence and visited the museums.
sentences.de: Wir blieben ein paar Tage in Florenz und besuchten die Museen. (a few = ein paar, positiv gemeint)

sentences.en: She drank some tea and ate a little bread.
sentences.de: Sie trank etwas Tee und aß ein wenig Brot. (a little = ein wenig, positiv gemeint)

parts: Anna is planning a party for her friends. She bought
questions.solutionEn: She bought some snacks and a few bottles of juice.
questions.solutionDe: Sie hat ein paar Snacks und ein paar Flaschen Saft gekauft.
questions.explain: some = bejahter Satz; a few + zählbares Nomen im Plural (bottles).
questions.read: Anna is planning a party for her friends. She bought some snacks and a few bottles of juice.

questions.solutionEn: She didn't buy much soda because many of her friends prefer water.
questions.solutionDe: Sie hat nicht viel Limonade gekauft, weil viele ihrer Freunde lieber Wasser trinken.
questions.explain: much + unzählbar (soda) in der Verneinung; many + zählbar (friends).
questions.read: She didn't buy much soda because many of her friends prefer water.

parts: vegetarian options yet. She still has
time to go to the supermarket.
questions.solutionEn: There are also a lot of sandwiches, but there aren't any vegetarian options yet. She still has a little time to go to the supermarket.
questions.solutionDe: Es gibt auch viele Sandwiches, aber noch keine vegetarischen Optionen. Sie hat noch ein wenig Zeit, um in den Supermarkt zu gehen.
questions.explain: a lot of im bejahten Satz; any in der Verneinung (aren't … any); a little + unzählbar (time).
questions.read: There are also a lot of sandwiches, but there aren't any vegetarian options yet. She still has a little time to go to the supermarket.

parts: honest people in the world these days.
questions.solutionEn: There aren't many honest people in the world these days.
questions.solutionDe: Es gibt heutzutage nicht viele ehrliche Menschen auf der Welt.
questions.explain: people = zählbar (Plural) → many. much nur bei unzählbaren Nomen.
questions.read: There aren't many honest people in the world these days.

parts: This man is a mystery. We have very
questions.solutionEn: We have very little information about his private life.
questions.solutionDe: Wir haben sehr wenig Informationen über sein Privatleben.
questions.explain: information = unzählbar → little. few nur bei zählbaren Nomen; a little wäre positiv („ein wenig“), hier ist „fast nichts“ gemeint.
questions.read: This man is a mystery. We have very little information about his private life.

parts: She isn't the most popular person in the class. She has very
questions.solutionEn: She has very few friends.
questions.solutionDe: Sie hat sehr wenige Freunde.
questions.explain: friends = zählbar → few (negativ: fast keine). a few wäre positiv („ein paar“).
questions.read: She isn't the most popular person in the class. She has very few friends.

parts: Our team is losing 1:0 but there is still
hope that they'll turn the game around.
questions.solutionEn: There is still some hope that they'll turn the game around.
questions.solutionDe: Es gibt noch etwas Hoffnung, dass sie das Spiel drehen.
questions.explain: Bejahter Satz → some. any nur in Frage/Verneinung.
questions.read: Our team is losing 1:0 but there is still some hope that they'll turn the game around.

parts: students have such good marks. She is an unmatched genius.
questions.solutionEn: Few students have such good marks.
questions.solutionDe: Nur wenige Schüler haben so gute Noten.
questions.explain: Gemeint ist „fast niemand“ → Few (negativ). A few („ein paar“) würde den Sinn abschwächen; little nur bei unzählbaren Nomen.
questions.read: Few students have such good marks. She is an unmatched genius.

parts: I've read only the first chapter, that's why I don't have
questions.solutionEn: I don't have much to say about the characters.
questions.solutionDe: Ich kann nicht viel über die Figuren sagen.
questions.explain: much in der Verneinung (nicht viel zu sagen) – „much“ steht hier allein (unzählbare Menge).
questions.read: I've read only the first chapter, that's why I don't have much to say about the characters.

parts: cake left! Ben's eaten the whole thing!
questions.solutionEn: There is no cake left! Ben's eaten the whole thing!
questions.solutionDe: Es ist kein Kuchen mehr übrig! Ben hat alles aufgegessen!
questions.explain: no + Nomen = kein (im bejahten Satzbau). any bräuchte eine Verneinung (isn't any); none steht ohne Nomen.
questions.read: There is no cake left! Ben's eaten the whole thing!

parts: patience? I'll be back in 5 minutes.
questions.solutionEn: Can I ask you for a little patience?
questions.solutionDe: Darf ich dich um ein wenig Geduld bitten?
questions.explain: patience = unzählbar → (a) little; positiv gemeint („ein wenig Geduld“) → a little.
questions.read: Can I ask you for a little patience? I'll be back in 5 minutes.

parts: Science doesn't interest me. It's the subject I know very
questions.solutionEn: It's the subject I know very little about.
questions.solutionDe: Es ist das Fach, über das ich sehr wenig weiß.
questions.explain: know little about = wenig wissen (unzählbar, negativ gemeint).
questions.read: Science doesn't interest me. It's the subject I know very little about.

parts: The party was ok but there wasn't
questions.solutionEn: The party was ok but there wasn't much dancing.
questions.solutionDe: Die Party war okay, aber es wurde nicht viel getanzt.
questions.explain: dancing = unzählbar, Verneinung → much. „a lot“ bräuchte „of“ vor einem Nomen und passt stilistisch in Verneinungen nicht.
questions.read: The party was ok but there wasn't much dancing.

parts: We'd better go to the petrol station. We've got very
questions.solutionEn: We've got very little petrol left.
questions.solutionDe: Wir haben nur noch sehr wenig Benzin.
questions.explain: petrol = unzählbar → little (negativ: fast nichts mehr). Nach „very“ steht nie „a little“.
questions.read: We'd better go to the petrol station. We've got very little petrol left.

parts: Tomorrow's party will be legendary! There'll be
questions.solutionEn: There'll be a lot of people!
questions.solutionDe: Da werden viele Leute sein!
questions.explain: Bejahter Satz + zählbares Nomen → a lot of. much nur bei unzählbaren Nomen in Frage/Verneinung.
questions.read: Tomorrow's party will be legendary! There'll be a lot of people!

parts: My wallet is empty. I have
questions.solutionEn: I have no money whatsoever.
questions.solutionDe: Ich habe überhaupt kein Geld.
questions.explain: no + Nomen = überhaupt kein. any bräuchte ein verneintes Verb (don't have any).
questions.read: My wallet is empty. I have no money whatsoever.

parts: In his new flat there is
furniture. Maybe one chair and a small table.
questions.solutionEn: In his new flat there is little furniture.
questions.solutionDe: In seiner neuen Wohnung gibt es wenig Möbel.
questions.explain: furniture = unzählbar (im Englischen!) → little. Achtung: „Möbel“ ist im Deutschen Plural, im Englischen aber uncountable.
questions.read: In his new flat there is little furniture. Maybe one chair and a small table.

parts: Her grades have improved greatly. She's made
questions.solutionEn: She's made a lot of progress.
questions.solutionDe: Sie hat große Fortschritte gemacht.
questions.explain: progress = unzählbar; bejahter Satz → a lot of. much wäre nur in Frage/Verneinung üblich.
questions.read: Her grades have improved greatly. She's made a lot of progress.

parts: Norway is a very rich country. There isn't
questions.solutionEn: There isn't much poverty.
questions.solutionDe: Es gibt nicht viel Armut.
questions.explain: poverty = unzählbar, Verneinung → much.
questions.read: Norway is a very rich country. There isn't much poverty.

parts: school subjects are easier than others.
questions.solutionEn: Some school subjects are easier than others.
questions.solutionDe: Manche Schulfächer sind leichter als andere.
questions.explain: Bejahter Satz → some (hier: „manche“).
questions.read: Some school subjects are easier than others.

parts: I could rely on him in the past but this time he offered me
questions.solutionEn: This time he offered me no help.
questions.solutionDe: Dieses Mal hat er mir keine Hilfe angeboten.
questions.explain: no + Nomen = kein/keine. Der Satz ist bejaht (offered), daher kein any.
questions.read: I could rely on him in the past but this time he offered me no help.

parts: The suspect was released because too
questions.solutionEn: Too little evidence was presented.
questions.solutionDe: Es wurden zu wenige Beweise vorgelegt.
questions.explain: evidence = unzählbar (im Englischen!) → little. „too little evidence“ = zu wenig Beweismaterial.
questions.read: The suspect was released because too little evidence was presented.

parts: things to do in Egypt that are free of charge.
questions.solutionEn: There aren't many things to do in Egypt that are free of charge.
questions.solutionDe: In Ägypten gibt es nicht viele Dinge, die gratis sind.
questions.explain: things = zählbar, Verneinung → many. no ginge nur ohne „aren't“ (There are no things …).
questions.read: There aren't many things to do in Egypt that are free of charge.

questions.solutionEn: How much money do you need?
questions.solutionDe: Wie viel Geld brauchst du?
questions.explain: money = unzählbar → how much.
questions.read: How much money do you need?

questions.solutionEn: How many apples do you want?
questions.solutionDe: Wie viele Äpfel willst du?
questions.explain: apples = zählbar (Plural) → how many.
questions.read: How many apples do you want?

questions.solutionEn: Do you have any milk left?
questions.solutionDe: Hast du noch Milch übrig?
questions.explain: Frage → any. (some nur in bejahten Sätzen oder bei Angeboten wie „Would you like some tea?“)
questions.read: Do you have any milk left?

questions.solutionEn: I bought some apples at the market.
questions.solutionDe: Ich habe am Markt ein paar Äpfel gekauft.
questions.explain: Bejahter Satz → some.
questions.read: I bought some apples at the market.
